context_requirements: Cell must express the targeted integrin heterodimer (e.g., alpha-v/beta-3, alpha-v/beta-5, alpha-5/beta-1) on the surface.
Cell must be adherent to an integrin-dependent extracellular matrix ligand (vitronectin, fibronectin, tenascin) for detachment-mediated signaling.
Cell must depend on integrin-mediated survival/proliferation signaling for a measurable transcriptional consequence.
Immortalized lines grown on plastic with serum may have weak matrix dependence, limiting response.
falsifiers: No change in any of the nine lines at 24 h for proliferation or apoptosis markers.
Strong, consistent upregulation of immediate-early or stress genes at 6 h across all lines.
A clear dose-independent or line-independent transcriptional signature identical to unrelated drug classes.
No apoptosis or proliferation-down signature in any line despite integrin expression.

evidence.supports: alpha-v integrin antagonist EMD 121974 induces apoptosis in alpha-v-expressing brain tumor cells by detaching them from vitronectin and tenascin.
alpha-v/beta-3 and alpha-v/beta-5 integrin antagonist S247 decreases colon cancer metastasis and angiogenesis in mice.
alpha-5/beta-1 integrin antagonist JSM6427 suppresses neovascularization and induces apoptosis of vascular endothelial cells.
pan-alpha-v integrin antagonist MK-0429 suppresses TGF-beta-induced fibrosis marker gene expression and reduces fibrosis in vivo.
cRGD integrin antagonist EMD121974 reduces proliferation and augments apoptosis in malignant glioma cells.

changes: No direction changes were required: the listed late_up genes are consistent with detachment/fibrosis/inflammation responses and the late_down genes are consistent with reduced integrin-dependent proliferation.
No specificity changes were required: the proximal lists are empty, so no generic proliferation or stress genes are present in proximal lists.
No line-response changes were required: the weak/none pattern is consistent with variable integrin expression and matrix dependence across the nine lines.
No kinetics or magnitude changes were required: slow kinetics and weak 24 h magnitude are consistent with detachment-mediated apoptosis and proliferation loss.
No evidence changes were required: all five cited abstracts support the stated claims.
